CmdUuid.description: A lower-case hyphenated UUID naming a record (doc 05 §3.2).

Dec3.description: A canonical decimal string: at most three fraction digits, no trailing fraction zeros, no leading zeros, no plus sign, no "-0", no exponent, no white space, no unit (doc 05 §3.2). The pattern bounds the integer part to 16 digits; the exact i64 range of the thousandths (about 9.2 x 10^15) is checked by the reader.

Ident.description: An identifier: non-empty, one line (no control character U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F to U+009F), without leading or trailing white space (the Unicode White_Space set); interior spaces are allowed (doc 05 §3.2). JSON Schema cannot express Unicode Normalization Form C; the reader rejects non-NFC text.

PartRef.description: A part on a device (doc 03 §7): the embedded copy and an optional part variant (FR-PRT-003).

copy.description: The copy ID of the embedded part, `v5(NS_LIBCOPY, library ‖ item)`.

variant.description: A variant key of the part.

PartUse.description: A part use on a device (ADR-0006): the part and its quantity in the part's order unit.

qty.description: The quantity in the part's order unit (pieces, metres, sets).

description:
`plc.set_module_part` (`SetModulePart`, FR-PLC-053, doc 10 §3.3 N1, §8 item 3): changes a module's part
and removes the channels the new part no longer has, after the confirmation that lists them.

Sets `Device.parts` to `parts` (absent: the parts stay as they are) and deletes the module's channels
numbered at or above the channel count of the resulting PLC section (the part use named by
`plc_module.part_use`, else the first part use whose part has a PLC section; a device without the
`plc_module` aspect, or whose part has no channel spec, has a count of 0). Their bindings, symbols and
comments are members of the channel record and go with it; no other record refers to a channel, and
exchange records do not exist yet (doc 10 §4). Normaliser N1 then creates the missing channels and applies
the part's channel kind, as for any part change.

**Bulk:** it always runs as a preview first (ADR-0008), and committing the preview is FR-PLC-053's
confirmation: the preview's diff lists every deleted channel, and its outcome has one notice per channel
with its number, binding and symbol. `fields.set` on `parts` stays the interactive way to change a part:
it never removes a channel, and N1 names the surplus channels it leaves, which this command without
`parts` removes. Rejected: a part copy that does not exist and a module that does not exist
([`CmdError::NotFound`]). A module whose parts and channels need no change gives an empty transaction,
which commits nothing. Undoable as one step. Outcome: the module.

parts.description:
The module's new part uses (the whole list, as `fields.set` on `parts` takes it); absent: the parts
stay and only the surplus channels are removed.

title: plc.set_module_part
